note: A word for a family member written twice is the word of a small child or an affectionate one: pi, grandmother, pipi, grandma; pa, father, papa, dad.
A verb written twice describes an ongoing action, as -ing in English: kap, cry, kapkap, crying; nui, laugh, nuinui, laughing.
The letter j is not used in native Zolai words; a keyword with it is a loanword, a name or a foreign spelling.

The negation lo becomes loh before the suffix na: hoih, good, hoihlohna, badness; dam, well, damlohna, sickness. hoihlona is not written.
A stem ending in sia becomes siat before the suffix na: hamsia, unfortunate, hamsiatna, misfortune. hamsiana is not written.
